blocks.en: They are BoPEP4, a Brassica oleracea plant elicitor peptide, LEA14, a late embryogenesis abundant protein, and ACC (1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate) deaminase. The binding sites themselves turned out to have almost no headroom, so the engineering moved to the construct and the delivery.

blocks.en: It is a record of what we got wrong and caught in time. A purification tag every earlier check had approved turned out, once simulated, to abolish the one contact the peptide depends on. The largest gain available on ACC deaminase, an enzyme, is a change to the medium it works in.

blocks.en: Three protectants, three sends. Each lane holds two boxes: what went out, with the reason protein design chose it and a link to the run it came from, and below it what was considered and rejected. The second box matters as much as the first, because what was ruled out, and on what evidence, is the other half of the result.

blocks.en: A 23-residue peptide that switches on the plant’s own stress response by binding a receptor, PEPR1. A shorter peptide is cheaper for the bioreactor to make, so the question was how much could be cut from the front before it stopped working. Nothing computational separated the best candidates, so the whole ladder went out and the concentration decides.

blocks.en: A 151-residue plant protein that helps cells survive drying and salt. It is not an enzyme: one copy protects one thing and is not reused, so the only ways to get more effect are to deliver more copies or make each copy do more. These five test both, by trimming the loose ends and by bolting on a membrane-binding motif it does not naturally have.
blocks.text: A 151-residue plant protein that helps cells survive drying and salt. blocks.en: Adds an ability LEA14 lacks. The K-segment sticks to membranes as a cell dries; LEA14 cannot do this on its own, so this asks whether borrowing it makes each copy count for more.

blocks.en: A bacterial enzyme that lowers plant stress by eating ACC, the molecule plants turn into the stress hormone ethylene. Unlike the other two it is a true catalyst, so one copy works over and over. That is why the decisive result here is not a mutation.
blocks.text: A bacterial enzyme that lowers plant stress by eating ACC, the molecule plants turn into the stress hormone ethylene. Unlike the other two it is a true catalyst, so one copy works over and over. That is why the decisive result here is not a mutation.

blocks.en: No mutant was sent. The enzyme meets far less ACC than it could handle, so how much working enzyme is present matters more than how good the enzyme is. On the modeling, the largest gain available is a change to the conditions it works in instead of to the protein, which is why no variant was ordered.
